replies.text:
Checks (step 2 items):
- Automated abuse of a reachable entry point (sign-in, email/SMS, mass sign-up, scraping): design has no such entry point — only "Payment events are published to a Kafka topic that every internal service can consume"; deterministic signals say `"auth":false`, exposure internal. Nothing to report.
- Staff/admin/moderator screens showing other people's content: design names no UI or screen at all, only a Kafka topic and consumers. Not present.
- Delete/moderate/refund/approve/role-change/money movement without a record: design describes publish and consume only; no actor-initiated action is described. Accountability of event origin is already covered by listed threat 5 ("no signature, producer identity or integrity hash").
- Personal/financial pages browsers, proxies or CDNs could store: no HTTP responses or documents in the design; data lives in a broker topic. Not present.
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV/spreadsheet exports, emails, headers or another interpreting system: the design states only that "Events include the card BIN, last four digits, amount and customer id" — no export, email or log sink is described; the spread of card data into consumer stores and logs is already listed threat 4.
- Single-reviewer threats: integrity/origin (1) duplicates listed 2 and 5; retention in topic logs and consumer copies (2) duplicates listed 4; producer identity (3) duplicates listed 5; earliest-offset replay of history (4) is the same weakness and same harm as listed 1 (every internal consumer reads card BIN, last four and customer id for every payment), so not a distinct gap.
